Sara —

Thanks for the detailed sheet; I mapped your monthly ingest and retention profile to two possible structures and attached a draft quote (redwood_quote_v3.pdf). High level — both options keep the same base SLA and dashboard entitlements:

Option A (Slab-first):
- Monthly RB slabs (0-5TB / 5-20TB / 20TB+) with step-down unit price as you cross thresholds.
- If you exceed a slab mid-month, excess is billed at the next slab per-GB rate (no instant spike surcharge).
- We offer a 10% overage credit for the first two months following pilot cutover to smooth ramp risk.

Option B (Buffer + Paygo):
- Smaller committed slab + pay-as-you-go beyond that with a soft cap for negotiated overage discount tiers.
- This gives a lower committed spend but higher marginal rates.

Tracing (hotpath vs coldpath):
- Hotpath: sampled traces / full-span retention required for debugging — included in dashboards package up to X spans/month.
- Coldpath: aggregated traces / low-cardinality telemetry — priced at a lower per-span rate.
- High-cardinality surcharge applies only if trace cardinality > 1M unique tag dimensions/month; otherwise covered by the hotpath allowance.

Quick ask: would Acme prefer predictability (Option A) or lower commitment (Option B) for year-one? If you want, I can draft a blended concession that stages credits as adoption grows.

Diego
